# 198 — PR explainer (HIGH tier: full walkthrough + quiz)

Verifier verdict: **PASS, 9/9 criteria, tier HIGH** — tier assigned independently by the verifier,
overruling the spec's own LOW guess. HIGH on **diff size alone** (arithmetic below); no trust rail,
router, parameterized-URL behaviour, dependency or config is touched.

## Goal

`prescanI18n()` in `audit-app.js` is the detector that asks "is the Korean actually Korean?". Item 190
built it. Item 198 fixes the predicate, which implemented **half** of the rule the team had already
written down for itself.

## The intuition, in one paragraph

The playbook's rule (`product-audit.md` class 5(2), written 2026-07-31) says a KO value is untranslated
if it is byte-identical to its EN twin **AND** contains no Hangul. Those two conjuncts are not
equivalent partners. "Contains no Hangul" is a property of **the KO value alone**. "Is identical to EN"
is a property of **the pair**. And a property of the pair goes silent exactly when the pair drifts:
reword the EN string without touching KO, and the two stop being identical — at precisely the moment
the KO value has become stale English. The shipped gate tested only the pair-property. It was a drift
detector that switches itself off on drift.

Probed against the real exported function before the fix (no fixtures — injected dictionaries through
`prescanI18n({dict})`):

| EN | KO | untranslated? | old gate | correct? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Powered by` | `Powered by` | yes | flagged | ✅ |
| `Powered by` | `Powered by ` (one trailing space) | yes | **clean** | ❌ miss |
| `Powered by` | `Powered by the DefiLlama feed` | yes | **clean** | ❌ miss |
| `Powered by` | `제공` | no | clean | ✅ |
| `$100` | `$100` | no — a bare figure | **flagged** | ❌ false positive |

## What changed, and why

**One line deleted is the whole fix.** `if (enVal !== koVal) continue;` — the pair-property gate — is
gone. What replaces it is a property of the KO value alone: no Hangul, **and** at least one Latin
letter, **and** not on the exact-key-path allowlist.

The Latin-letter conjunct is the part worth arguing with, and it is an **addition** not asked for by
the spec's "Change" section. It exists because the spec's own acceptance criterion 4 demands it:
dropping the identity gate makes *every* no-Hangul KO value a suspect, including legitimately
non-linguistic ones (`"$100"`, `"2026"`, `"—"`), each of which would then need an allowlist entry it
should never have needed — and criterion 6 explicitly bans allowlisting non-brand strings. Requiring at
least one Latin letter restricts suspects to values that actually carry translatable English prose.
The blind spot it accepts is stated in the code, the notes and the playbook: an untranslated KO value
made purely of digits/punctuation is undetectable. That is acceptable, because such a value carries no
English prose to be stale.

Byte-identity is not discarded — it is **demoted from gate to detail**. When it happens to hold, the
finding still says so, because it is real and useful information. It just no longer decides whether the
finding exists.

## The diff, in reading order

1. **`audit-app.js:857-870`** — new `I18N_LATIN_LETTER = /[A-Za-z]/`, with the rationale and the
   accepted blind spot in the comment rather than in a commit message nobody will read again.
2. **`audit-app.js:871-891`** — `I18N_IDENTICAL_ALLOWLIST` renamed to `I18N_UNTRANSLATED_ALLOWLIST`.
   The old name asserted the thing that is no longer true: the gate does not key on sameness. **No
   entry was added or removed** — 24 in, 24 out. Grep-confirmed there is no importer outside
   `audit-app.js` and `test_audit_i18n_parity.js`, so no compat alias was kept.
3. **`audit-app.js:974-997`** — the Rule 2 comment and predicate. One `continue` deleted, one added,
   one `identical` ternary feeding the detail string.
4. **`audit-app.js:1009`, `4123-4131`** — the rename at `emptyI18nResult()` and the export block.
5. **`test_audit_i18n_parity.js`** — the header narrative, the mechanical rename, and five test changes:
   - **inverted** the old test `'a KO value that differs from EN is NOT reported, even with no Hangul'`.
     It asserted the bug. It is now the reworded-English case, asserting the finding fires.
   - **added** the trailing-space miss, which asserts inline that the fixture is *not* byte-identical —
     so the test documents the class it closes rather than merely passing.
   - **added** the `$100` false-positive case, asserting both that it is not a suspect and that it needs
     no allowlist entry.
   - **added** the positive control on **real historical bytes**: `git show 648401297:translations.js`
     (the parent of `dc2f947cc`, "190: nothing checked whether the Korean was Korean") written to a temp
     file, `require()`d, fed to the real function, asserting both `landing.footerPoweredBy` and
     `landing.footerMadeWith` fire. A hand-written fixture is authored from the same mental model that
     missed the bug; historical bytes are not. If `git show` fails it throws a loud named failure —
     never a silent skip.
   - **added** (post-verifier, see below) the conjunct-source test.
6. **`product-loop-kit/playbooks/product-audit.md`** — class 5(2) rewritten in place to state the
   shipped predicate, plus a genuine typo fix: the playbook's Hangul class read `/[가-힯…]/` (U+D7AF)
   where the code has always read `/[가-힣…]/` (U+D7A3). Aligned to the code.

## This ships a gate, not a repair — and says so

There is **no live instance** in the dictionary today. Measured: `{"scanned":543,"suspectCount":0,`
`"allowlistSize":24,"suspects":[]}`. Of 390 shared string leaves, 24 have no Hangul, 24 are
byte-identical, and they are **the same 24** — every one a brand (`Claude Pro`, `Spotify`,
`DefiLlama API`, …) or an acronym (`TVL`, `APY`, `LP/DEX`, `RWA`), all allowlisted with a stated reason.
A true negative is worthless until it is proven able to return non-zero, which is what the historical
positive control and the three miss-case tests are for.

## Verification

- `node test_audit_i18n_parity.js` → **17 passed, 0 failed**.
- `node test_audit_prescan.js` → **51/0**; `node test_audit_app.js` → **3/0**. Both re-run by the
  operator and again by the verifier; neither needed killing inside the 5-minute timebox.
- Non-vacuity, **one sub-rule at a time** (a single combined mutation cannot distinguish two working
  rules from one working rule and one dead one). Baseline/restore `md5sum audit-app.js` =
  `9cc2a918676cfa7c2da4c7c44d1dfcbe` every cycle:
  - Hangul class neutered → 2 red (a mixed Hangul+Latin fixture, and the real dictionary flooding with
    ~50 genuinely-Korean strings that contain a Latin acronym).
  - Latin-letter conjunct neutered → 1 red, exactly the `$100` false-positive test.
  - allowlist lookup neutered → 3 red (the two allowlist tests plus the real dictionary, all 24 brands).
- The verifier ran its own mutations, different in kind: an allowlist prefix-match (correctly caught
  red), and a commit-ish swap on the positive control (failed loudly, not silently — confirming it reads
  real history).

## The verifier's finding, fixed before merge

The verifier's third mutation **swapped the conjunct's argument** rather than deleting the guard:
`I18N_LATIN_LETTER.test(koVal)` → `test(enVal)`. **The suite stayed green, 16/16.** Nothing pinned down
*which* value that conjunct must read. The shipped code was already correct, so this was never a live
bug — but an unpinned rule can be silently killed by a future edit, which is the exact class this item
exists to close. Shipping it would have reproduced the item's own thesis as a defect.

Fixed **test-only** (`audit-app.js` byte-identical, md5 unchanged) with a 17th test whose fixture
inverts the sides: EN `"$100"` (no Latin letter), KO `"Powered by"` (Latin letters, no Hangul). The
correct rule fires; the mutated rule drops the finding. Replayed by the operator: **16 passed, 1
failed**, the one red being exactly that test; restored byte-identical, 17/17 green.

Sequencing stated plainly rather than glossed: the verifier's PASS was issued against the 16-test diff.
The 17th test is an additive, test-only strengthening of acceptance criterion 7 that the verifier itself
surfaced. No product code changed after the verdict; the tier is unaffected.

## Risk tier arithmetic (why HIGH)

`git diff --numstat origin/main`: `audit-app.js` 47+18 = 65, `test_audit_i18n_parity.js` 119+15 = 134
at verification time → **199 lines** against the LOW lane's 150-line cap, counting test lines per the
item-166 precedent. (The 17th test adds ~22 more.) No trust rail (`APY_SANITY_LIMIT`, `DEFAULT_MIN_TVL`,
anomaly flags, degen haircut), no `home.html` router or `?token=/?chain=/?pool=` behaviour, no generated
SEO surface, no dependency, no `package.json`, no config. **Size alone disqualifies LOW.** Nothing on
the NEVER list, so autonomy (c) permits the merge.

Scope confirmed by the verifier: only `audit-app.js`, `test_audit_i18n_parity.js`, the playbook and the
notes changed. **`translations.js` is byte-untouched** — editing it would turn this into a user-facing
copy item requiring EN + natural KO together (spec §73, an automatic FAIL). `package.json` untouched;
`test_audit_i18n_parity.js` was already registered in `test:serial` (grepped, not assumed).

**No human visual spot-check needed:** detector-only, no render path, no user-facing surface.

## Measurement

`i18n.suspectCount` stays 0 with no growth in `allowlistSize` for non-brand/non-acronym reasons.
Window 14 days, to **2026-08-15**. Keep if the gate stays clean and the allowlist does not grow to
accommodate ordinary prose. **REVERT-CANDIDATE** if it fires on legitimate Korean — a false positive on
real KO text means the character class is wrong, so widen the class, never allowlist the string.

No north-star measurement is possible or claimed: pre-traffic product-quality work under the 2026-07-23
standing decision.

## Quiz

1. The playbook's rule had two conjuncts and the shipped gate implemented one. Why is
   "byte-identical to EN" the *wrong* one to keep, and what makes the failure worst in exactly the
   scenario the gate exists for?
2. EN `Powered by` / KO `Powered by ` (one trailing space). What did the old predicate do with it, what
   does the new one do, and what does the shipped test assert *beyond* "it fires now"?
3. The Latin-letter conjunct is not in the spec. What forces it, what would happen without it, and what
   blind spot does it knowingly accept?
4. How many allowlist entries were removed when the predicate was re-derived, and why is that number
   the honest answer rather than a missed cleanup?
5. The verifier's mutation that the suite *survived* — what was it, why was it not a live bug, and why
   was it still worth an extra test before merge?
